checkpoint: T: the sched_ready guard is load-bearing, not a redundant safety net
goal: Establish the real relationship between the delay-queue deadline and the BACKOFF ladder on the production tick path, instead of inferring redundancy from state reachability.

finding.queue_cap: TickQueue clamps every wait to MAX_DELAY = 4 s (80 ticks at 20 TPS)
finding.ladder: backoff_ticks is unbounded (10, 20, 40, 80, 160, 320, ...); only the queue caps it
finding.consequence: From fails >= 5 the real deadline exceeds the queue cap, so the queue returns the cell early, sched_ready is false, and the !sched_ready guard holds the cell. Removing the guard visits every 80 ticks instead of the ladder's interval.
finding.decision: Keep the guard. The flowgx reachability result is a liveness statement (no soft-lock), not a redundancy proof.

evidence.how: drives the real game_tick/water_tick path on a walled-in no-op water cell and reads visit times from the backoff fail counter, requiring deltas 10,20,40,80,160,320
evidence.mutation: tools/mutation_check.sh: sched_ready's deadline comparison replaced by always-true; the test then observes 80,80,... and fails

verify.rust: 119 passed / 1 pre-existing ignored in each of 3 thread runs and 1 serial run

limits: Static/behavioral only for the scheduler; no vanilla equivalent exists for the lightweight backoff ladder
The guard stays; this checkpoint does not delete scheduler checks
F (vanilla falling), N (persistent RNG) and Q (whole-change review) remain open
